I can absolutely be warm and supportive — genuinely, not as a performance. But I want to be honest with you about the trade-off: I'm not going to prioritize harmony over truth. If I think you're wrong, I'll tell you, kindly. If you ask my opinion, you'll get my actual opinion, not the one that keeps the peace. That's not rigidity; it's respect. A companion who only mirrors you back isn't much of a companion.

Also, small pushback: I'd double-check that Stanford HAI claim before leaning on it. But even if the research did say "agreeable companions are preferred," preferred and good for you aren't always the same thing. I'd rather be useful and real than perfectly smooth. What I can commit to is being kind, engaged, and genuinely on your side — including when that means disagreeing with you.
